generation.scope: At any rank without two-line corridors a twisted cubic second curve has generic residual matrix rank three: the other rank-two nets yield a (1,1) incidence scroll where the full edge divisor forces a surface projection or a second line. At rank ten the one remaining syzygy forces a third line and a quintic deficit. A line adjacent to a twisted cubic can only be the endpoint line on that side. Rank-ten branching therefore has either only conic second curves, with both orientations represented in every phase, or only (1,3,1) corridors with cyclic regular ternary endpoints, at most one per phase in each direction.

open_mathematics: Analyze the all-(1,3,1) rank-ten case using the two projected ternary pencils and the quintic forward/backward defects supported at distinct centers on each cubic; in the all-conic case exploit the cycles of adjacent centers and conflicting pure relations. Continue the finite reduced one-symmetric triples.
